---
title: "External Tool"
description: "A function or service outside a model that an AI application can invoke to perform a defined operation."
term: "External Tool"
letter: "E"
category: "AI Agents"
difficulty: "Beginner"
---

## Simple explanation

An external tool lets an AI application perform an operation beyond
generating text, such as searching a database, calculating a value, or
calling an API.

## Technical explanation

A tool is typically exposed through a name, description, input schema,
and execution function or service. A model may request a tool call, while
application code validates the request, checks authorization, executes
the operation, and returns a result. The application—not the model
alone—controls access and side effects.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Tools connect models to current information and real system capabilities.
They also create security, reliability, and privacy considerations:
arguments need validation, permissions should be scoped, and consequential
actions may require confirmation.

## How it works

The application provides a set of allowed tools and their descriptions.
The model may select a tool and propose structured arguments. The
application validates and executes the call, then returns the result to
the model or user. Errors and authorization failures should be handled
explicitly.

## Practical example

An assistant can call a read-only product-search API to find matching
items, then summarize the returned results. A separate confirmation step
would be appropriate before placing an order.

## Common misconceptions

- A model's tool-call proposal is not itself execution; application code
  must perform and authorize the operation.
- Tool descriptions and schemas do not replace runtime validation.
- Giving an agent a tool does not guarantee that it will use it correctly.
